Formula: De Morgan's Laws
Exact Expression: \neg(P \wedge Q) \iff (\neg P \vee \neg Q) \quad \text{and} \quad \neg(P \vee Q) \iff (\neg P \wedge \neg Q)
Definitions: Pair of transformation rules in formal logic and set theory relating conjunction and disjunction through logical negation.
Derivation/Reference: Augustus De Morgan, Formal Logic (1847); anticipated by Aristotle and William of Ockham
Example: not (Rain AND Weekend) = (not Rain) OR (not Weekend)
Domain: logic
Assumptions: Classical Boolean logic / Boolean algebra with Law of Excluded Middle
Common Errors: Failing to negate the individual operands when changing AND to OR
subject: De Morgan's Laws
